metadata.title: RxJS Deep Dive: Stream Signature Reference
metadata.attribution: These definitions and teaching notes were created with the help of GPT-6 Astra, under the course direction of Hans Schenker.
metadata.notationSummary: Cω-inspired stream shorthand that translates into ordinary TypeScript types. It is explanatory notation, not syntax accepted by the TypeScript compiler.
legend: A, B
Input and output payload types. S is accumulated state; K is a key; O is an opening-signal payload; R is a registration token; D is a default-value type.
A*
Observable<A>: a stream with zero or more next values per subscription. The type does not promise values, completion, a clock, or shared execution.
Optional occurrence refinements: zero or one / exactly one / one or more next values. State the lifetime and termination assumptions. Ordinary Observable<A> does not enforce these bounds.
An array value / an Observable whose next values are arrays.
A tuple of two sources / a stream of two-value tuples.
An outer stream whose next values are inner streams.
A => B
A value function; in TypeScript write (value: A) => B.
A source-to-result transformation; in TypeScript write (source: Observable<A>) => Observable<B>.
Input<A>
ObservableInput<A>: Observable, promise-like, iterable, async iterable, array-like, interoperable Observable, or readable-stream-like input.
A stream whose next values can belong to either payload type.
A & B
A value satisfying both structural requirements; used for a group stream with a key property.
never*
No next payload values. Completion, error, or remaining open must be described separately.
Notice<A>
ObservableNotification<A>: { kind: "N"; value: A } | { kind: "E"; error: unknown } | { kind: "C" }.
param?: Type
An optional configuration parameter. This question mark is parameter syntax, not the stream-cardinality suffix.
globalNotes: The cards show selected common forms. Callback indices, some optional parameters, and the exhaustive overload sets live in the linked API and pinned source.
Creation functions return Observables directly. Most pipeable functions return transformations used by pipe; partition and connectable forms have explicitly different result shapes.
Unless a card says otherwise, next, error, complete, and unsubscription are separate concerns. Unsubscription is not a complete notification.

Examples omit imports and generally show Observable expressions, not subscribe calls. Their next/complete comments describe a subscription allowed to finish; external-request outcomes remain conditional.
Durations normally use milliseconds with asyncScheduler. A supplied scheduler can provide a different or virtual clock. Integer counts and positive concurrency limits are the teaching defaults.
null and undefined are ordinary emitted values. of(undefined) emits once; EMPTY emits no next values.
An operator factory builds a description. Work starts through subscription, although argument expressions and eager input creation may already have run.
Shorthand describes type shape. Read the adjacent behavior policy and execution details before claiming two operators are equivalent.

categoryIntros.Creation Operators: Start from values, callbacks, events, requests, or a clock. Read when work begins and how the subscription ends.
categoryIntros.Join Creation Operators: Supply all sources directly. Tuple joins preserve positions; union joins forward values from different sources.
categoryIntros.Transformation Operators: Change payloads, accumulate state, group values, or choose an Action Policy for inner subscriptions.
categoryIntros.Filtering Operators: Choose which values pass. Similar A* => A* shapes can have very different gates, deadlines, and completion rules.
categoryIntros.Join Operators: Combine a primary source with companions, or flatten an outer stream. Read who triggers output and when inner subscriptions start.
categoryIntros.Multicasting Operators: Choose how listeners share source connections and what later listeners receive. Type shape alone does not specify this policy.
categoryIntros.Error Handling Operators: Choose whether an error terminates, selects another input, or requests another subscription.
categoryIntros.Utility Operators: Observe execution, schedule work or delivery, measure time, enforce deadlines, or convert notifications.
categoryIntros.Conditional and Boolean Operators: Answer questions about a subscription. Many answers require completion; a counterexample can sometimes end the search early.
categoryIntros.Mathematical and Aggregate Operators: Produce a final aggregate when the source completes. Compare with scan when learners need every intermediate state.

glossary: SchedulerLike
A scheduler supplies now() and scheduling operations. It can represent real or virtual time; choosing one does not imply another thread.
TimestampProvider
A clock object with now(): number. It measures time and need not schedule work.
ThrottleConfig
An object with optional leading and trailing booleans. Defaults: leading true, trailing false.
RetryConfig / RepeatConfig
Retry uses count?, delay?, resetOnSuccess?; repeat uses count? and delay?. Retry count means retries after the original run; repeat count means total runs.
ShareConfig<A>
Selects a connector and resetOnError, resetOnComplete, and resetOnRefCountZero policies. Each reset can be a boolean or a callback returning a reset notifier.
ShareReplayConfig
Requires refCount in the typed object form; bufferSize, windowTime, and scheduler are optional. Prefer explicit bounded buffering and an explicit refCount decision.
ConnectConfig<A>
A selector-sharing configuration with a required connector factory returning a SubjectLike<A>.
ConnectableConfig<A>

An explicit-connection configuration with a required connector when an object is supplied, and optional resetOnDisconnect. This name comes from the implementation; it is not a root-exported RxJS 7.8.2 type.
Connectable<A>
An Observable<A> that also exposes connect(): Subscription. The modern connectable() factory returns this shape.
ConnectableObservable<A>
The legacy connectable class shape, carrying older connection and refCount machinery. It is distinct from the minimal modern Connectable<A> interface.
Subject<A> / SubjectLike<A>

A Subject can receive next/error/complete and be subscribed to as an Observable. SubjectLike names the structural observer-and-subscribable contract. Its subtype determines replay and terminal behavior.
Observer<A> / Subscription / Unsubscribable
An Observer handles next/error/complete. A Subscription manages teardown. Unsubscribable is the smaller contract with unsubscribe(): void.
GroupedObservable<K, A>
An Observable<A> with a key: K property. The shorthand (A* & { readonly key: K }) preserves both stream shape and the group key.
TimeoutConfig<A, B*> / TimeoutInfo<A>
TimeoutConfig names first?, each?, scheduler?, with?, and meta?. TimeoutInfo carries meta, seen, and lastValue. The shorthand specializes its fallback ObservableInput parameter to B*.
Notice<A>
The structural N/E/C notification union defined in the legend. materialize returns Notification instances compatible with that union; dematerialize accepts the structural union.
AjaxConfig / AjaxResponse<A>
AjaxConfig chooses the XMLHttpRequest request and progress options. AjaxResponse<A> is the wrapper whose response field contains A; selecting a type does not validate a server response.
WebSocketSubjectConfig<A> / WebSocketSubject<A>
The config supplies connection, serialization, and deserialization options. The result is both a stream of received A values and an outgoing next(value) interface.
EventTarget / AddEventListenerOptions
The selected DOM event target and its capture, once, and passive listener options. fromEvent also supports other event-source protocols.
Request / RequestInit / Response
The platform fetch request, request-options, and response types. The response body is consumed separately unless the fromFetch selector includes it.
Date
A JavaScript absolute date value, interpreted by the relevant operator against its supplied clock.
Record<string, A> / A[K] / keyof A
A string-keyed record; the value type at property K; and the permitted property-key types of A. Known-property shorthand assumes K extends keyof A.
Exclude<A, B> / readonly
Exclude removes union members assignable to B; readonly forbids assignment through that property in TypeScript. Neither performs runtime validation.

operators.name: ajax
operators.behavior: Start an XMLHttpRequest on subscription and emit response objects containing a payload of type A. With the default progress settings, a successful request emits its response and completes.
details: Each subscription creates a request. Defaults include GET, asynchronous operation, and JSON response decoding.
Network errors, timeouts, and HTTP statuses of 400 or above use the error channel.
Unsubscribing aborts an unfinished request.
Enabling upload or download progress adds response-shaped progress emissions; ajax is therefore not universally a one-value stream.
operators.example:
ajax<{ name: string }>('/api/profile')
// On a successful default request: next an AjaxResponse whose response is the profile; complete.
operators.overloads: A names the decoded response payload, not the entire response wrapper; the type argument performs no runtime validation. ajax.getJSON<A>(url): A* selects only the response body. GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE helpers and AjaxConfig provide request options.

operators.name: bindCallback
operators.signature: bindCallback(fn: (arg: A, callback: B => void) => void): A => B*
operators.behavior: Turn a callback API into a function that returns a stream of its result. Calling the bound function prepares that stream; its first subscription invokes the original function.
details: For a normal single-result callback, emit its result and complete when the callback resolves.
Subscribers to the same returned Observable share one invocation and receive its cached result, including late subscribers. Calling the bound function again creates a separate result stream.
Unsubscribing removes this observer; it does not supply a cancellation mechanism to the callback API.
operators.example:
const double = (n: number, done: (result: number) => void) => done(n * 2);
bindCallback(double)(3) // next: 6; complete synchronously
operators.overloads: Shown for one input argument and one callback result. Real signatures preserve arbitrary argument tuples; several result arguments become one tuple, while no result arguments produce one undefined value. An optional scheduler controls invocation and delivery; a result-selector form also exists.

operators.name: bindNodeCallback
operators.signature: bindNodeCallback(fn: (arg: A, callback: (error: unknown, value: B) => void) => void): A => B*
operators.behavior: Adapt a Node-style error-first callback. A successful callback supplies the result value; an error argument terminates the stream through the error channel.
details: Only null or undefined in the error slot means success; other values count as errors.
The original function runs on the first subscription to each returned Observable. That Observable shares and caches its callback result for later subscribers.
This adapter does not automatically cancel the underlying operation when a subscriber unsubscribes.
operators.example:
const lengthOf = (s: string, done: (err: Error | null, n: number) => void) => done(null, s.length);
bindNodeCallback(lengthOf)('RxJS') // next: 4; complete synchronously
operators.overloads: Shown for one input and one success result. Real signatures preserve argument tuples; multiple success results become one tuple, and no success result produces undefined. Optional scheduler and result-selector forms are available.

operators.name: defer
operators.behavior: Run the factory separately for each subscription, convert its result to an Observable, and forward that execution.
details: The factory runs when subscribed, not when defer is called.
A thrown factory error becomes an error notification.
A promise created inside the factory starts at subscription time. Returning an already-created promise does not restart its work.
operators.example:
const value$ = defer(() => of(Math.random()));
// Each subscription draws a new number, emits it, and completes.
operators.overloads: The factory can return any ObservableInput, including an Observable, promise, array, or iterable.

operators.name: empty
operators.behavior: Create a stream that completes without emitting a value.
details: Without a scheduler, this returns EMPTY and completes synchronously on subscription.
With a scheduler, schedule the completion notification; unsubscribing first cancels that scheduled completion.
operators.example: empty() // no next values; complete synchronously
operators.overloads: This function is deprecated in RxJS 7.8.2. EMPTY expresses the usual immediate form.
operators.replacement: EMPTY; for scheduled completion, scheduled([], scheduler).

operators.name: from
operators.behavior: Convert an Observable-compatible input into a stream of its values. The input kind determines how those values become available.
details: Arrays and synchronous iterables emit their items synchronously by default, then complete when exhausted.
A promise emits its resolved value and completes, or reports its rejection as an error. Its underlying work may already have started.
An existing Observable retains its execution behavior. Unsubscribing from a promise conversion stops delivery but does not cancel the promise itself.
operators.example: from([1, 2, 3]) // next: 1, 2, 3; complete synchronously
operators.overloads: Input<A> includes Observable, interoperable Observable, promise-like, array-like, iterable, async iterable, and readable-stream-like inputs. The scheduler-argument overload is deprecated; use scheduled(input, scheduler).

operators.name: fromEvent
operators.signature: fromEvent(target: EventTarget, eventName: string, options?: AddEventListenerOptions): A*
operators.behavior: Turn events from a target into values. In the common DOM form, each event object becomes one emitted value.
details: Each subscription installs its own listener; unsubscription removes that listener.
An event source does not complete merely because no more events arrive.
DOM options such as once affect the listener; once does not send an RxJS complete notification.
operators.example:
fromEvent<MouseEvent>(document, 'click')
// next: each click event; unsubscribe removes this listener
operators.overloads: Shown for a DOM EventTarget with an explicitly selected event type A. Node-style and jQuery-style emitters and collections of targets are also supported. Multiple event-handler arguments are emitted as one array; result-selector forms can project them.

operators.name: fromEventPattern
operators.signature: fromEventPattern(addHandler: (handler: A => void) => R, removeHandler?: (handler: A => void, token: R) => void): A*
operators.behavior: Adapt an event API by supplying the functions that attach and detach a handler. Every handler call supplies an emission.
details: addHandler runs for each subscription. Its return value is a registration token, passed to removeHandler together with the same handler during teardown.
If removeHandler is omitted, this adapter cannot detach the registration for you.
Events continue until the subscription ends; the adapter has no automatic completion signal.
operators.example:
fromEventPattern<Event>(
  handler => document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', handler),
  handler => document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', handler)
) // next: visibility events; unsubscribe detaches the handler
operators.overloads: Shown for a handler receiving one A and a registration token R, which may be void. Several handler arguments become one array, while zero handler arguments become an empty array. An optional result selector can map the handler arguments.

operators.name: generate
operators.signature:
generate(options: {
  initialState: S,
  condition?: S => boolean,
  iterate: S => S,
  resultSelector: S => A,
  scheduler?: SchedulerLike
}): A*
operators.behavior: Generate a sequence by repeatedly testing a state, projecting a value, and advancing the state. Stop when the condition becomes false.
details: The condition is checked before emitting from the initial state and before every later state.
Without a scheduler, the loop runs synchronously; an unbounded loop can occupy the current call stack until unsubscribed or interrupted by an error.
A supplied scheduler schedules iteration. Each subscription starts again from initialState.
operators.example:
generate({ initialState: 1, condition: n => n <= 3, iterate: n => n + 1, resultSelector: n => n * n })
// next: 1, 4, 9; complete synchronously
operators.overloads: Without resultSelector, emit the state itself: S*. Omitting condition generates without a condition-based stopping point. The older positional-argument overloads are deprecated; the options-object form is current.

operators.name: interval
operators.behavior: Emit an increasing counter at a recurring interval, starting with 0 after the first period.
details: Defaults are period = 0 and asyncScheduler; a negative period is treated as 0.
Each subscription starts its own counter and scheduled work.
It has no natural completion. Unsubscribing cancels its scheduled work.
operators.example:
interval(1000).pipe(take(3))
// next: 0, 1, 2 on successive one-second periods; then complete
operators.overloads: Periods use milliseconds with the default scheduler; actual delivery follows the selected scheduler and host timing.

operators.name: of
operators.behavior: Emit the supplied argument values in order, then complete. Each argument stays a single value.
details: By default, emission and completion happen synchronously during subscription.
Arrays, promises, null, and undefined are emitted as values; of does not unpack them.
With no arguments, complete without a next value.
operators.example: of([1, 2], [3]) // next: [1, 2], [3]; complete synchronously
operators.overloads: For heterogeneous arguments, A is their union. Scheduler-argument overloads are deprecated; use scheduled(values, scheduler) when scheduling these values is intended.

operators.name: range
operators.behavior: Emit count numbers, starting at start and increasing by 1, then complete.
details: The common form emits synchronously during subscription.
A count of zero or less produces an empty completion; use nonnegative integer counts for the intended counting contract.
Downstream unsubscription stops the loop before later values are emitted.
operators.example: range(3, 3) // next: 3, 4, 5; complete synchronously
operators.overloads: The single argument is the count: range(3) starts at 0 and emits 0, 1, 2. The scheduler-argument overload is deprecated; scheduled(range(start, count), scheduler) schedules observable subscription and delivery.

operators.name: throwError
operators.behavior: Create a stream that reports an error as soon as it is subscribed.
details: The factory runs for each subscription, so an error object can be created at the point of execution.
The result emits no next values and terminates with error, rather than complete.
operators.example: throwError(() => new Error('Failed')) // no next values; error: Failed
operators.overloads: The overload accepting an error value directly and the scheduler-argument overload are deprecated. The error factory form is current.

operators.name: timer
operators.signature: timer(due: number | Date, scheduler?: SchedulerLike): number*
operators.behavior: Wait until the due time, emit 0, and complete. A separate repeating form continues with an increasing counter.
details: A numeric due time is relative to subscription; a Date is interpreted against scheduler.now(). Past due times are treated as zero delay.
The default scheduler is asyncScheduler, so timer(0) schedules its emission rather than behaving like synchronous of(0).
timer(startDue, period, scheduler?) emits 0 at the start time and then 1, 2, ... at that period; a nonnegative period makes it recurring.
Unsubscribing cancels the scheduled work. The repeating form has no natural completion.
operators.example: timer(1000) // after the scheduled delay: next 0; complete
operators.overloads: Shown for the one-shot overload, whose runtime value is 0; the public TypeScript payload type is number. The repeating overload also returns number*. A negative interval duration is treated as a one-shot timer in 7.8.2.

operators.name: iif
operators.signature: iif(condition: () => boolean, whenTrue: Input<A>, whenFalse: Input<B>): (A | B)*
operators.behavior: Choose one of two inputs at subscription time and forward that chosen execution.
details: Evaluate condition for every subscription and subscribe only to the selected input.
Constructing the branch arguments still follows normal JavaScript evaluation. Wrap branch work in defer when its creation must also wait.
A thrown condition error goes to the error channel.
operators.example: iif(() => true, of('yes'), of('no')) // next: 'yes'; complete
operators.overloads: Both branches accept ObservableInput. The result payload is the union of their value types.

operators.name: animationFrames
operators.signature: animationFrames(timestampProvider?: TimestampProvider): ({ timestamp: number, elapsed: number })*
operators.behavior: Emit a timing record on each animation frame. elapsed measures the time since this subscription began.
details: Uses requestAnimationFrame; each subscription has its own frame loop and starting time.
Without a custom provider, timestamp comes from the animation-frame callback and elapsed uses performance timing.
A custom TimestampProvider supplies the current time used for both fields. Unsubscription cancels the pending frame request.
operators.example:
animationFrames().pipe(take(2))
// next: timing records for two animation frames; then complete
operators.overloads: Requires an environment with animation-frame support. It does not complete by itself.

operators.name: EMPTY
operators.behavior: An Observable constant that completes immediately without emitting a value.
details: Each subscription receives a synchronous complete notification.
It differs from of(undefined), which emits one undefined value before completing.
operators.example: EMPTY // when subscribed: no next values; complete synchronously
operators.overloads: Use this constant for immediate empty completion; scheduled([], scheduler) makes completion scheduled.

operators.name: fromFetch
operators.signature: fromFetch(input: string | Request, init?: RequestInit): Response*
operators.behavior: Start a fetch request per subscription. In the default form, emit the Response when it is available and then complete; reading its body is a separate step.
details: HTTP error status codes still produce Response values; inspect response.ok or response.status when deciding whether to treat them as errors.
Network failures and abort failures use the error channel.
Unsubscribing while the fetch is pending aborts it. In the default form, automatic abort stops once the Response has been delivered.
The selector form keeps the request abortable while the selected input, such as response.json(), is being consumed.
operators.example:
fromFetch('/api/profile', { selector: response => response.json() })
// On successful JSON decoding: next the decoded body; complete
operators.overloads: With init.selector: Response => Input<A>, the result is A*. Use that form to include body consumption in the subscription's lifetime; the return type of response.json() itself does not validate a domain schema.

operators.name: never
operators.behavior: Return NEVER: a stream that sends no notifications and has no natural termination.
details: The returned subscription stays open until it is unsubscribed or another operator ends it.
This legacy function and the NEVER constant describe the same behavior.
operators.example: never() // when subscribed: no next, no error, no complete
operators.overloads: The function is deprecated in RxJS 7.8.2.

operators.name: NEVER
operators.behavior: An Observable constant that sends no next, error, or complete notifications.
details: A subscription remains open until explicitly unsubscribed or ended by another operator.
The type never* says only that there are no next values; the absence of completion is this constant's behavior.
operators.example:
NEVER.pipe(takeUntil(timer(1000)))
// no next values; complete when the timer emits

operators.name: pairs
operators.signature: pairs(object: Record<string, A>, scheduler?: SchedulerLike): [string, A]*
operators.behavior: Emit the own enumerable string-keyed entries of an object as key-value tuples, then complete.
details: The implementation calls Object.entries when pairs is called, so the entry array is captured before subscription.
Without a scheduler, emit the entries synchronously on subscription. Symbol keys and inherited properties are not included.
The tuples hold the original property values; referenced objects are not deeply copied.
operators.example: pairs({ a: 1, b: 2 }) // next: ['a', 1], ['b', 2]; complete
operators.overloads: Shown for a homogeneous string-keyed record. The legacy API has additional input overloads and an optional scheduler. Its implementation uses Object.entries rather than consuming an iterable protocol.
operators.replacement: from(Object.entries(object)); use scheduled(Object.entries(object), scheduler) for scheduled delivery.

operators.name: scheduled
operators.behavior: Convert an input into an Observable while using the supplied scheduler to control its consumption and delivery.
details: For Observable inputs, subscription and notifications are scheduled. For arrays and synchronous iterables, element production is scheduled.
The scheduler determines timing; queueScheduler can run work synchronously, while other schedulers defer it.
Scheduling a promise conversion does not defer the work that created the already-existing promise, and unsubscription does not cancel that promise.
operators.example:
scheduled([1, 2], asyncScheduler)
// scheduled next: 1, 2; then scheduled complete
operators.overloads: Accepts ObservableInput, including async iterables and readable streams. This replaces many deprecated scheduler-argument overloads on creation functions.

operators.name: using
operators.signature: using(resourceFactory: () => (Unsubscribable | void), observableFactory: (Unsubscribable | void) => (Input<A> | void)): A*
operators.behavior: Create a resource for a subscription and pass it to a factory that supplies that subscription's values. Dispose the resource when the established execution is torn down.
details: Both factories run separately for each subscription. The resource exposes an unsubscribe method; the factory may also return no resource.
After setup succeeds, completion, error, or downstream unsubscription disposes the resource. A void Observable-factory result acts like EMPTY.
In 7.8.2, cleanup is registered after observableFactory returns: if that factory throws after allocating the resource, provide cleanup for that failure path yourself.
operators.overloads: The actual Observable factory can return any ObservableInput, or void. The displayed resource contract is the API's Unsubscribable | void type.

operators.name: webSocket
operators.behavior: Create a duplex WebSocket endpoint: subscribing receives A values, while calling next sends A values to the server.
details: The first subscription opens the socket; subscribers to the same WebSocketSubject share that connection. When its last observer unsubscribes, it closes the socket.
Outgoing values sent before the socket opens are queued. Sending a value does not also emit it locally as an incoming value.
The default serializer uses JSON.stringify and the default deserializer uses JSON.parse; configure them for a different wire format.
A clean socket close completes its observers; an unclean close or socket error errors them.
operators.overloads: WebSocketSubject<A> is both an A* read side and an Observer<A> write side, so reducing the return type to A* would hide its duplex behavior. Configuration supports custom serialization, deserialization, lifecycle observers, and a WebSocket constructor.

operators.name: combineLatest
operators.behavior: After every source has supplied its first value, emit a tuple of the latest values whenever any source supplies another value.
details: Subscription order matters for synchronous inputs: earlier sources can emit several times before the later sources are subscribed.
A completed source keeps its last value available. The result completes when all sources have completed; any source error terminates the result.
RxJS 7.8.2 still waits for all completions when a source completes empty. Therefore combineLatest([EMPTY, NEVER]) neither emits nor completes.
With zero sources, complete without a next value.
operators.example:
combineLatest([of(1, 2), of('a', 'b')])
// next: [2, 'a'], [2, 'b']; complete
operators.overloads: Shown for two Observable inputs. Any-length tuples, arrays, and keyed records are supported, and inputs may be ObservableInput. A record produces a record of latest values. Positional-source and scheduler-argument forms are deprecated.

operators.name: concat
operators.behavior: Subscribe to the sources in sequence. Forward all values from the current source and move to the next only after it completes.
details: A source that never completes prevents later sources from being subscribed.
An error ends the sequence immediately; subsequent sources are not started.
With no sources, complete without a next value. No scheduler is added by the common form.
operators.example: concat(of(1, 2), of(3)) // next: 1, 2, 3; complete
operators.overloads: Any number of ObservableInput sources can be passed as separate arguments. concat(...sources) joins an array of streams; concat(sources) instead treats that array as one input and emits its elements. A legacy scheduler overload is also available.

operators.name: forkJoin
operators.behavior: Wait for all sources to complete, then emit one tuple containing each source's last value and complete. Every source must have supplied a value.
details: If any source completes empty, the result completes without a next value and tears down active subscriptions.
Otherwise, a source that never completes prevents the final tuple, even if it has already emitted.
A source error terminates the result and tears down the other active inputs.
With zero sources, complete without a next value.
operators.example: forkJoin([of(1, 2), of('a', 'b')]) // next: [2, 'b']; complete
operators.overloads: Shown for a pair of Observables. Tuples of any length, arrays, and keyed records are supported; actual inputs may be ObservableInput. Positional-source overloads are deprecated. The result emits at most one tuple in the selected form.

operators.name: merge
operators.signature: merge(first: A*, second: B*, concurrent?: number): (A | B)*
operators.behavior: Forward values from active sources as they arrive. Several sources may be subscribed at the same time.
details: Concurrency defaults to Infinity. A positive concurrency limit delays subscriptions to excess sources until active ones complete.
Inputs are subscribed in argument order; synchronous earlier inputs can finish before later subscriptions begin.
Complete when all sources finish. An error terminates the result and tears down active inputs; zero sources complete empty.
operators.example: merge(of(1, 2), of('a')) // next: 1, 2, 'a'; complete
operators.overloads: Shown for two sources; any number of ObservableInput sources can be supplied. Pass a trailing positive number to set concurrency. Scheduler-argument overloads are deprecated.

operators.name: partition
operators.signature: partition(source: A*, predicate: A => boolean): [A*, A*]
operators.behavior: Return two streams: one passes values for which the predicate is true, and the other passes values for which it is false.
details: This is a pair of Observables, not an Observable that emits pairs.
Each branch subscribes to the input independently. Subscribing to both can run a cold source twice and evaluate the predicate separately.
partition does not introduce sharing; arrange sharing explicitly if both branches must observe one source execution.
operators.example:
const [even$, odd$] = partition(of(1, 2, 3, 4), n => n % 2 === 0);
// even$: 2, 4, complete; odd$: 1, 3, complete (separate subscriptions)
operators.overloads: The actual input may be ObservableInput, and predicates receive an index. A type-guard predicate narrows the true branch to B and the other branch to Exclude<A, B>. The standalone function is current; the old pipeable partition is deprecated.

operators.name: race
operators.behavior: The first next value selects the source whose subsequent values are forwarded. A completion or error before any next ends the result immediately.
details: Once a source wins with a value, unsubscribe the other active candidates and follow the winner through its completion or error.
Sources are subscribed in order. A synchronous winner or terminal notification can prevent later sources from ever being subscribed.
Unlike most join creators, race([]) stays open without next values in RxJS 7.8.2.
operators.example:
race([of('first'), of('second')])
// next: 'first'; complete; the second source is never subscribed
operators.overloads: Array and separate-argument forms accept any number of ObservableInput sources. The output payload is the union of source payloads.

operators.name: zip
operators.behavior: Match values by position: first with first, second with second, and so on. Emit a tuple only when every input has supplied its next unmatched value.
details: Faster sources wait in per-source queues; this can retain many values when rates differ.
Complete once a completed input has no buffered value left, because another full tuple is then impossible.
A source error terminates the result and tears down the other inputs. With zero inputs, complete without next values.
operators.example:
zip([of(1, 2, 3), of('a', 'b')])
// next: [1, 'a'], [2, 'b']; complete; unmatched 3 is discarded
operators.overloads: Any-length tuple and separate-argument forms accept ObservableInput sources. A result-selector overload maps each matched tuple to another payload type.

operators.name: onErrorResumeNext
operators.behavior: Run sources one after another, moving to the next after either completion or error. Values pass through; source errors do not.
details: A normally completing source also advances to the next one; this is not a fallback that runs only on error.
An error from a source is swallowed, so this operator cannot inspect it or choose recovery based on it.
A source that never ends blocks the remaining sources. Once all sources have ended, complete; an empty list completes immediately.
operators.example:
onErrorResumeNext([of(1), throwError(() => new Error('skip')), of(2)])
// next: 1, 2; complete; the intermediate error is swallowed
operators.overloads: Array and separate-argument forms accept ObservableInput sources. This standalone creator is current. Use onErrorResumeNextWith for the current pipeable form.

operators.name: buffer
operators.behavior: Collect source values into an array. Each closing notification emits the current array and starts an empty replacement.
details: A closing next can emit an empty array; closing-notifier completion does not close the buffer or complete the result.
Source completion emits the remaining array, including an empty one, then completes. Errors and unsubscription discard pending values.
In RxJS 7.8.2 the source is subscribed before the closing notifier, which matters for synchronous sources.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(buffer(NEVER)) // next: [1, 2, 3]; complete
operators.overloads: The closing notifier can be any ObservableInput; the shorthand shows an Observable whose payload is ignored.

operators.name: bufferCount
operators.behavior: Collect values into arrays and emit each array when it reaches the chosen size.
details: With positive counts, the default start interval is bufferSize, producing consecutive batches. A smaller interval overlaps buffers; a larger interval leaves gaps.
Source completion emits all remaining partial buffers, then completes. An empty source produces no arrays.
Buffers open when a source value arrives. Errors and unsubscription discard unfinished buffers.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3, 4, 5).pipe(bufferCount(2)) // next: [1, 2], [3, 4], [5]; complete
operators.overloads: Passing null for startBufferEvery also selects bufferSize. The teaching form assumes positive buffer and start counts.

operators.name: bufferTime
operators.behavior: Collect values during each time span and emit the resulting array when that span ends.
details: The first buffer opens on subscription. With the displayed form, each emitted buffer is immediately replaced; even empty buffers are emitted.
The default clock is asyncScheduler and durations are in milliseconds. The operator schedules boundaries, while source values retain their arrival order within each buffer.
Source completion flushes every active buffer immediately, then completes; it does not wait for their timers. Errors and unsubscription discard active buffers and cancel their timers.
The longer forms can create overlapping buffers or gaps, and can close a buffer early at maxBufferSize. Without a creation interval, early closure immediately starts a replacement.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(bufferTime(100)) // next: [1, 2, 3] immediately on source completion; complete
operators.overloads: Also accepts (timeSpan, creationInterval, scheduler?) and (timeSpan, creationInterval, maxBufferSize, scheduler?). The creation interval defaults to no separate opening schedule and maxBufferSize to Infinity.

operators.name: bufferToggle
operators.signature: bufferToggle(openings: O*, closingSelector: O => unknown*): A* => (A[])*
operators.behavior: Each opening value starts a buffer and selects its closing notifier. That notifier's first next emits the buffer.
details: Several buffers can be open together; a source value is added to all of them. Values arriving while no buffer is open are omitted.
Closing-notifier completion alone leaves its buffer open. Completion of openings only prevents further openings.
Source completion emits all still-open buffers, including empty ones, then completes. An error fails the result; unsubscription releases source and notifier subscriptions.
Openings are subscribed before the source, so a synchronous opening can establish a buffer before a synchronous source starts.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(bufferToggle(of('open'), () => NEVER)) // next: [1, 2, 3]; complete
operators.overloads: Both openings and the closing-selector result can be ObservableInput values. The selector receives the opening payload, not a source payload.

operators.name: bufferWhen
operators.behavior: Open one buffer immediately. Each selected closing next emits that buffer, opens its replacement, and calls the selector again.
details: Only one buffer is active at a time. The closing subscription is replaced after its first next; completion without a next leaves the current buffer open.
Source completion emits the remaining buffer, including an empty array, then completes. Errors and unsubscription discard it.
The first closing notifier is subscribed before the source. A selector that repeatedly returns an immediately emitting source can keep reopening buffers synchronously.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(bufferWhen(() => NEVER)) // next: [1, 2, 3]; complete
operators.overloads: The closing selector may return any ObservableInput. Unlike windowWhen, closing-notifier completion does not advance the buffer.

operators.name: concatMap
operators.behavior: Process source values in order, one inner subscription at a time. Wait for the current inner to complete before starting the next.
details: While an inner is active, source values queue. The projector is called when each queued value gets its turn, not when that value first arrives.
Outer completion waits for the active inner and queued work. An inner that never completes blocks the queue.
Errors terminate the result and tear down active subscriptions; downstream unsubscription also abandons queued work.
The queue can grow when arrivals outpace completion. This is mergeMap with concurrency 1, without an added scheduling or sharing policy.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(concatMap(n => of(n, n * 10))) // next: 1, 10, 2, 20; complete
operators.overloads: The projector also receives a zero-based processing index and can return any ObservableInput. The legacy resultSelector overload is deprecated; concatMap itself is current.

operators.name: concatMapTo
operators.behavior: For each source value, subscribe to the same supplied inner Observable, waiting for each subscription to complete before starting the next.
details: Source payloads are ignored, but each source next reserves a turn in the queue.
A cold inner starts its execution again for each subscription; a hot inner exposes whatever values arrive during that subscription.
Outer completion waits for queued turns and the active inner. Errors or downstream unsubscription terminate the active work and abandon the queue.
operators.example: of('a', 'b').pipe(concatMapTo(of(1, 2))) // next: 1, 2, 1, 2; complete
operators.overloads: The supplied inner may be any ObservableInput. The legacy resultSelector form also exists but is deprecated; the entire concatMapTo API is deprecated.

operators.name: exhaust
operators.behavior: Subscribe to an arriving inner only while idle. Ignore arriving inners until the current one completes.
details: This is the deprecated name of exhaustAll, with identical behavior.
Ignored inners are neither subscribed nor queued. A synchronous inner can complete before the outer emits the next inner, allowing both to run.
Outer completion waits for the accepted inner to complete. Errors and downstream unsubscription tear down active work.
operators.example: of(timer(10), of(99)).pipe(exhaust()) // next: 0 after the timer; complete; of(99) is ignored
operators.overloads: The outer can emit any ObservableInput; the shorthand shows an Observable of Observables.

operators.name: exhaustMap
operators.behavior: While idle, project a source value and subscribe to its inner. Ignore further source values until that inner completes.
details: Ignored values are not queued and do not call the projector. Only accepted values advance the projector's index.
A never-completing inner keeps the operator busy indefinitely. A synchronous inner may finish before the next source value arrives.
Outer completion waits for the active inner. Source, projection, or inner errors fail the result; downstream unsubscription tears down active work.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(exhaustMap(n => of(n).pipe(delay(10)))) // next: 1; complete; 2 and 3 are ignored while busy
operators.overloads: The projector also receives a zero-based accepted-value index and may return any ObservableInput. Only the legacy resultSelector overload is deprecated.

operators.name: expand
operators.signature: expand(project: A => A*, concurrent?: number): A* => A*
operators.behavior: Emit each source value and recursively project every value reached. Values produced by inner streams become further inputs to the same projection.
details: The starting source values are included in the output. Returning EMPTY ends that branch without removing the value that led to it.
The default concurrency is Infinity. A finite positive limit queues values until an inner subscription slot becomes available; projection and output order depend on that limit and inner timing.
Completion requires the source, all recursive inner work, and the queue to finish. Errors or downstream unsubscription tear down active subscriptions.
There is no built-in visited set or cycle detection. A projection that keeps producing values can continue indefinitely.
operators.example: of(1).pipe(expand(n => n < 4 ? of(n + 1) : EMPTY)) // next: 1, 2, 3, 4; complete
operators.overloads: Shows recursion within one payload type A. The projector also receives an index and may return ObservableInput. The legacy scheduler argument is deprecated; schedule inner subscriptions with subscribeOn when needed.

operators.name: groupBy
operators.signature: groupBy(key: A => K): A* => (A* & { readonly key: K })*
operators.behavior: Route each value into the stream for its key. Emit a new keyed stream when that key first appears, then send matching values through that stream.
details: A group is a GroupedObservable: an Observable with a key property. Default groups use Subjects, are hot, and do not replay missed values; subscribe when the group is emitted.
Without a duration selector, groups remain tracked until the source terminates. A duration next or completion expires that group; a later value with the same key creates a new group.

Source, key-selector, and element-selector errors reach the outer stream and all groups. A duration-stream error affects its own group; source completion completes all current groups and the outer stream.
Subscribed groups can keep the source subscription alive after the outer group stream is unsubscribed. Teardown waits for the remaining group subscriptions to end.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3, 4).pipe(groupBy(n => n % 2), mergeMap(group => group.pipe(toArray(), map(values => ({ key: group.key, values }))))) // next: { key: 1, values: [1, 3] }, { key: 0, values: [2, 4] }; complete
operators.overloads: The options form can select element payloads, group duration, and a custom connector. With element: A => B, the result is (B* & { readonly key: K })*. A type-guard key has narrowing overloads. Legacy positional element/duration/connector overloads are deprecated; groupBy itself is current.

operators.name: map
operators.behavior: Apply the projection to each source value and emit its returned value.
details: Projection runs during each source next; map adds no scheduling step.
If the projection returns an Observable, that Observable is the payload. It is not automatically subscribed or flattened: the resulting shape is (B*)*.
A thrown projection error fails the result. Otherwise, source completion and errors pass through.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(map(n => n * 10)) // next: 10, 20, 30; complete
operators.overloads: The projector also receives a zero-based source index. The thisArg overload is deprecated; map itself is current.

operators.name: mapTo
operators.behavior: Replace every source value with the same supplied value.
details: Source next notifications determine when the constant is emitted; source payloads are ignored.
The supplied value is reused. An object is the same reference on every emission, and an Observable value is emitted without being subscribed.
An empty source produces no constant value. Source completion and errors pass through.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(mapTo('saved')) // next: 'saved', 'saved'; complete
operators.overloads: The public input type is unknown because the source payload is unused.

operators.name: mergeMap
operators.signature: mergeMap(project: A => B*, concurrent?: number): A* => B*
operators.behavior: Project source values into inner streams and forward their values as they arrive. Several inner subscriptions may be active together.
details: Concurrency defaults to Infinity. With a finite positive limit, excess source values queue and the projector is called only when a subscription slot opens.
Output follows inner emission order, which can differ from source order. With concurrency 1, the processing policy is concatMap.
Outer completion waits for active inners and queued work. Errors fail the result and tear down active subscriptions; downstream unsubscription also abandons queued values.
A concurrency limit bounds active inners, not the queue. Queued source values can accumulate when arrivals outpace inner completion.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(mergeMap(n => of(n).pipe(delay(n === 1 ? 20 : 10)))) // next: 2, 1 with these delays; complete
operators.overloads: The projector also receives a zero-based processing index and may return any ObservableInput. The legacy resultSelector overload is deprecated; mergeMap itself is current.

operators.name: mergeMapTo
operators.signature: mergeMapTo(inner: B*, concurrent?: number): A* => B*
operators.behavior: For each source value, subscribe to the same supplied inner and merge the values from those subscriptions.
details: Source payloads are ignored. Concurrency defaults to Infinity; a finite positive limit queues source triggers until a slot is available.
Each trigger creates another subscription. A cold inner can repeat its work, while multiple subscriptions to a hot inner can forward the same event more than once.
Outer completion waits for active and queued subscriptions. Errors or downstream unsubscription end active work and abandon the queue.
operators.example: of('a', 'b').pipe(mergeMapTo(of(1, 2))) // next: 1, 2, 1, 2; complete
operators.overloads: The supplied inner may be any ObservableInput. The legacy resultSelector form is also deprecated.

operators.name: mergeScan
operators.signature: mergeScan(accumulator: (S, A) => S*, seed: S, concurrent?: number): A* => S*
operators.behavior: Use the current state and an input to start an inner stream of states. Merge all active inners, remembering each emitted state for the next accumulator call.
details: The seed initializes state but is not emitted. The accumulator sees the latest inner value emitted so far, or the seed if no inner has emitted.
Concurrency defaults to Infinity. Overlapping accumulations can start from the same state, and a later emission from an older inner can replace a newer state.
With concurrency 1, queued inputs call the accumulator after prior inners complete, using the latest state at that moment. This serializes asynchronous state transitions.
Outer completion waits for inners and queued work. State belongs to each subscription, but a supplied object seed is not cloned.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(mergeScan((state, n) => of(state + n), 0)) // next: 1, 3, 6; complete
operators.overloads: The accumulator also receives a zero-based processing index and may return ObservableInput<S>. There is no unseeded overload.

operators.name: pairwise
operators.behavior: Starting with the second source value, emit the previous and current values as a tuple.
details: The tuple order is [previous, current]. Adjacent tuples overlap in one value.
A source with zero or one value emits no pair. There is no final incomplete tuple when the source completes.
Only the previous value is retained between notifications; each pair is a new array, while its element references are unchanged.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(pairwise()) // next: [1, 2], [2, 3]; complete

operators.name: partition
operators.behavior: Return two streams: values that pass the predicate and values that fail it.
details: This legacy rxjs/operators form returns an array of streams, not an Observable emitting arrays. It ends the ordinary Observable pipeline at that point.
Each branch subscribes to the source separately and runs its own predicate evaluation. A cold source can execute twice when both branches are subscribed.
Sharing is a separate decision. With a hot source, each branch observes only values available during its own subscription.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(partition(n => n % 2 === 0)) // returns [passing$, failing$]; subscribing yields 2 / 1, 3; each completes
operators.overloads: Import this legacy form from rxjs/operators. The predicate also receives a zero-based index and an optional thisArg is supported. Prefer the current static partition from rxjs.

operators.name: pluck
operators.replacement: map(value => value?.property), with optional chaining for nested paths
operators.behavior: Read a property from every source value and emit the selected property value.
details: A nested path walks successive properties. If the path cannot be resolved, the operator emits undefined rather than omitting that input.
A selected null value is still an emitted value. Getter exceptions fail the result, just as a thrown map projection would.
Calling pluck with no property names throws when the operator is created.
operators.example: of({ name: 'Ada' }, { name: 'Erik' }).pipe(pluck('name')) // next: 'Ada', 'Erik'; complete
operators.overloads: Shows one known key, K extends keyof A, with the indexed property type A[K]. Typed overloads support nested paths; a general string path returns unknown. Real runtime data with missing properties can produce undefined.

operators.name: scan
operators.signature: scan(reducer: (S, A) => S, seed: S): A* => S*
operators.behavior: Update the current state with each source value and emit that updated state.
details: The seed supplies the first state but is not emitted on subscription. An empty source produces no state values.
Each subscription tracks its own state variable. A supplied object seed is reused by reference, so pure reducers should return the intended next state without mutating shared seed data.
Reduction runs when each input arrives. A thrown reducer error fails the result; source completion does not emit an extra final state.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(scan((state, n) => state + n, 0)) // next: 1, 3, 6; complete
operators.overloads: Shows the seeded form with one state type S. Without a seed, the first source value becomes state and is emitted without calling the reducer. Other overloads distinguish initial and accumulated state types. The reducer also receives the source index; explicitly passing undefined still supplies a seed.

operators.name: switchScan
operators.signature: switchScan(accumulator: (S, A) => S*, seed: S): A* => S*
operators.behavior: Use the current state and each input to select an inner stream of states. Replace the previous inner, forwarding and remembering values only from the active one.
details: The seed is not emitted. State is the latest inner value already emitted, so a canceled inner that emitted nothing has not advanced state.
On each new input, the prior inner is unsubscribed before the new accumulator call. Values already emitted by that inner remain part of the observed history.
Outer completion waits for the current inner. Errors or downstream unsubscription tear down active work.
State tracking is per subscription, but the supplied seed object is not cloned. The underlying work stops on cancellation only when the inner's teardown stops it.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(switchScan((state, n) => of(state + n).pipe(delay(10)), 0)) // next: 2; complete; the first inner never emits
operators.overloads: Shows one state type S. The accumulator also receives the source index and may return ObservableInput. There is no unseeded overload.

operators.name: switchMap
operators.behavior: For each input, replace the current inner subscription with the projected inner. Forward values from the active inner only.
details: The previous inner is unsubscribed before the next projector call and subscription. Previously emitted values are not undone.
Outer completion waits for the current inner to complete; an outer next, not outer completion, triggers replacement.
Unsubscribing stops observing the old inner. Stopping its underlying request, timer, or other work depends on that inner's teardown.
Inner streams determine emission timing. switchMap adds no sharing, and source, projection, or inner errors fail the result.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(switchMap(n => of(n).pipe(delay(10)))) // next: 2; complete; the first inner is canceled
operators.overloads: The projector also receives the source index and may return any ObservableInput. The legacy resultSelector overload is deprecated; switchMap itself is current.

operators.name: switchMapTo
operators.behavior: Each source value cancels the current inner subscription and starts another subscription to the same supplied inner.
details: Source payloads are ignored. A cold inner starts again; a hot inner supplies the events available to its replacement subscription.
Cancellation does not undo earlier emissions, and stopping underlying work depends on the inner's teardown.
Outer completion waits for the current inner. Errors or downstream unsubscription terminate active work.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(switchMapTo(timer(10))) // next: 0 from the replacement timer; complete
operators.overloads: The supplied inner may be any ObservableInput. The legacy resultSelector form is also deprecated.

operators.name: window
operators.behavior: Emit a live window stream immediately. Each boundary next completes that window and emits a new one.
details: Windows are hot and do not replay past values. Subscribe to each window when it is emitted, commonly by immediately flattening or processing it.
Boundary completion alone does not close the window or complete the result. Source completion completes the current window and the outer stream.
Source or boundary errors error both the current window and the outer stream. Downstream unsubscription tears down the source and boundary subscriptions.
The initial window is emitted before source subscription; the boundary subscription is established after the source subscription in RxJS 7.8.2.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(window(NEVER), mergeMap(w => w.pipe(toArray()))) // next: [1, 2, 3]; complete
operators.overloads: The boundary source may be any ObservableInput. Its next payload is ignored; it supplies window boundaries only.

operators.name: windowCount
operators.behavior: Divide source values into live window streams, completing each window after its chosen number of values.
details: For positive counts, the default start interval equals windowSize. Smaller intervals overlap windows; larger intervals leave values outside any window.
Windows are hot and need timely subscriptions. Each window is emitted when it opens, before its values arrive.
RxJS 7.8.2 opens the initial window immediately and eagerly opens each next window after the start interval. An empty source or an exact count boundary can therefore leave an empty window.
Source completion completes all open windows and the outer stream; source errors error them. Window completion does not wait for consumers to subscribe.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3, 4).pipe(windowCount(2), mergeMap(w => w.pipe(toArray()))) // next: [1, 2], [3, 4], []; complete
operators.overloads: The displayed behavior assumes positive windowSize. An omitted or nonpositive startWindowEvery uses windowSize.

operators.name: windowTime
operators.behavior: Emit a live window for each time span. In the displayed form, completing one timed window immediately opens the next.
details: A window is emitted when it opens, starting immediately on subscription. It is hot and does not replay missed source values.
The default scheduler is asyncScheduler, with millisecond durations. Timers close windows; source arrivals supply their values, and windows can be empty.
Source completion completes active windows immediately and completes the outer stream. Source errors error both; unsubscription cancels source and scheduled boundary work.
Longer forms support overlapping windows, gaps, and a maximum value count. Without a separate creation interval, hitting the count limit immediately opens a replacement.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(windowTime(100), mergeMap(w => w.pipe(toArray()))) // next: [1, 2, 3] immediately on source completion; complete
operators.overloads: Also accepts (timeSpan, creationInterval, scheduler?) and (timeSpan, creationInterval, maxWindowSize, scheduler?). The creation interval defaults to no separate opening schedule and maxWindowSize to Infinity.

operators.name: windowToggle
operators.signature: windowToggle(openings: O*, closingSelector: O => unknown*): A* => (A*)*
operators.behavior: Each opening value creates and emits a live window. Its selected closing notifier completes that window on the first next.
details: Windows can overlap or leave gaps. A source value is sent to every open window; with no open window it is omitted.
Closing-notifier completion alone does not close a window. Completion of openings prevents new openings without completing current windows.
Windows are hot and require timely subscriptions. Openings are subscribed before the source, allowing synchronous openings to establish windows first.
Source completion completes all current windows and the outer stream. Errors fail the outer stream; downstream unsubscription tears down source and notifier subscriptions.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(windowToggle(of('open'), () => NEVER), mergeMap(w => w.pipe(toArray()))) // next: [1, 2, 3]; complete
operators.overloads: Openings and closing-selector results may be ObservableInput values. The selector receives the opening value rather than the source value.

operators.name: windowWhen
operators.behavior: Open and emit a window immediately. A selected closing next or completion closes it, opens a replacement, and calls the selector again.
details: Only one window is active at a time. Unlike bufferWhen, a closing notifier that completes without a value also advances the window.
Windows are hot and do not replay past values. Subscribe when each is emitted to observe its contents.
Source completion completes the current window and outer stream. Source, selector, or closing errors error the window and the result; unsubscription tears down the active subscriptions.
The first closing notifier is subscribed before the source. Repeated immediately emitting or completing closers can reopen windows synchronously without letting the source run.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(windowWhen(() => NEVER), mergeMap(w => w.pipe(toArray()))) // next: [1, 2, 3]; complete
operators.overloads: The closing selector may return any ObservableInput.

operators.name: flatMap
operators.signature: flatMap(project: A => B*, concurrent?: number): A* => B*
operators.behavior: Project values to inner streams and merge their emissions. This is the deprecated alias of mergeMap.
details: Concurrency defaults to Infinity. A finite positive limit queues source values until an inner subscription can start.
Output follows inner emission timing, so source order is not guaranteed. Outer completion waits for active and queued work.
Errors or downstream unsubscription end active subscriptions and abandon queued work, exactly as with mergeMap.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(flatMap(n => of(n, n * 10))) // next: 1, 10, 2, 20; complete
operators.overloads: Inherits mergeMap's ObservableInput projector, processing index, concurrency option, and legacy deprecated resultSelector overloads.

operators.name: audit
operators.behavior: The first value starts a duration. While that duration is active, remember the latest source value; emit it when the duration sends a next notification.
details: New source values replace the pending value without restarting the active duration.
Duration completion without a next notification closes the duration without emitting the pending value.
Source completion waits for an active duration: a duration next releases the pending value before completion, while a duration completion without next discards it.
A source or duration error terminates the result and discards the pending value.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(audit(() => timer(10))) // next: 3 when the duration signals; complete
operators.overloads: The duration selector also accepts other ObservableInput values, including promises. Its emitted payload is ignored.

operators.name: auditTime
operators.signature: auditTime(duration: number, scheduler?: SchedulerLike): A* => A*
operators.behavior: The first value opens a timed interval. Emit the latest value at the end of that interval, then wait for another source value to open the next interval.
details: Values arriving during an interval replace the pending value without moving its deadline.
Intervals are started by source values; there is no continuously running sampling clock.
Source completion waits for an active interval and its pending emission. An error or downstream unsubscription discards that pending value.
The scheduler defaults to asyncScheduler; duration is measured in its time units, normally milliseconds.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(auditTime(10)) // next: 3 after the interval; complete
operators.overloads: Equivalent to audit(() => timer(duration, scheduler)).

operators.name: debounce
operators.behavior: Each source value replaces the pending value and starts a new duration. Emit that value if its duration sends a next notification before another source value arrives.
details: Every new source value unsubscribes the previous duration and chooses a replacement duration.
Duration completion without next does not release the pending value.
Source completion immediately emits any pending value and then completes, even if the duration has not signaled.
An error or downstream unsubscription discards the pending value.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(debounce(() => timer(10))) // next: 3 immediately on source completion; complete
operators.overloads: The duration selector also accepts other ObservableInput values. The duration payload is ignored.

operators.name: debounceTime
operators.signature: debounceTime(dueTime: number, scheduler?: SchedulerLike): A* => A*
operators.behavior: Wait for a quiet period after a source value, then emit the latest pending value. Each new value moves the deadline.
details: A continuously busy source can keep replacing the pending value without producing output.
Source completion immediately releases the pending value and then completes; it does not wait out the remaining delay.
A source error or downstream unsubscription discards the pending value.
The scheduler defaults to asyncScheduler; dueTime uses its time units, normally milliseconds.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(debounceTime(10)) // next: 3 immediately on source completion; complete
operators.overloads: The output remains A*: the operator can emit many values across separate quiet periods.

operators.name: distinct
operators.signature: distinct(keySelector?: A => K, flushes?: unknown*): A* => A*
operators.behavior: Emit a source value only when its selected key has not been seen in this subscription since the last flush.
details: Without a key selector, the source value itself is the key. Keys are stored in a JavaScript Set: objects compare by identity and repeated NaN keys count as duplicates.
A flushes next notification clears the remembered keys; flushes completion alone does not clear them or complete the result.
The remembered set can grow for the lifetime of a subscription; supplying a key selector does not impose a size limit.
operators.example: of(1, 1, 2, 1, 3, 2).pipe(distinct()) // next: 1, 2, 3; complete
operators.overloads: K is the selected key type. The optional flushes input also accepts other ObservableInput values.

operators.name: distinctUntilChanged
operators.behavior: Emit the first value, then emit a later value only when the comparator says it differs from the last emitted value.
details: Comparator true suppresses the new value; comparator false emits it and updates the remembered value.
The default comparator is ===. It does not perform a deep object comparison.
Suppressed values do not replace the comparison baseline; only the last emitted value is remembered.
operators.example: of(1, 1, 2, 2, 1).pipe(distinctUntilChanged()) // next: 1, 2, 1; complete
operators.overloads: The key-selector form is distinctUntilChanged(compare: (K, K) => boolean, keySelector: A => K): A* => A*. It compares selected keys but emits the original A values.

operators.name: distinctUntilKeyChanged
operators.signature: distinctUntilKeyChanged(key: K, compare?: (A[K], A[K]) => boolean): A* => A*
operators.behavior: Emit the first object, then suppress objects whose chosen property compares equal to that property on the last emitted object.
details: The default comparison is ===; a custom comparator returning true suppresses the new object.
The entire object is emitted, including properties that were not compared.
The previous object is retained by reference, so mutating it can change a later comparison.
operators.example: of({ id: 1 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }).pipe(distinctUntilKeyChanged('id')) // next: { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }; complete
operators.overloads: K extends keyof A; A[K] is the type of the selected property.

operators.name: elementAt
operators.behavior: Emit the value at a zero-based position, then complete and unsubscribe from the source.
details: At most one value is emitted. Counting begins with the first value observed by this subscription.
If the source completes before that position exists, the selected form errors with ArgumentOutOfRangeError.
A negative index throws when elementAt is called, before subscription.
operators.example: of('a', 'b', 'c').pipe(elementAt(1)) // next: 'b'; complete
operators.overloads: Use a non-negative integer index. Providing defaultValue: D changes the output to (A | D)* and emits the default on normal completion if the position was not reached.

operators.name: filter
operators.behavior: Keep each source value whose predicate returns true. Other values contribute no output.
details: The predicate is evaluated independently for each source value; a rejection does not stop later values from being tested.
Values that pass are forwarded during the source notification; filter adds no scheduling step.
The full result is A*: an individual input can contribute zero or one value, but the subscription can emit many values.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3, 4).pipe(filter(n => n % 2 === 0)) // next: 2, 4; complete
operators.overloads: The callback also receives a zero-based index. A type guard (value: A) => value is B, with B extends A, produces B*. Boolean has a truthiness-narrowing overload. Only overloads accepting thisArg are deprecated.

operators.name: first
operators.behavior: Emit the first matching value and complete immediately. Without a predicate, the first source value matches.
details: Once a match is emitted, the source subscription is closed; later values are not needed.
If the source completes without a match, the selected form errors with EmptyError.
An input that never matches and never completes can keep the result open without emitting.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(first(n => n > 1)) // next: 2; complete
operators.overloads: A second argument defaultValue: D changes the output to (A | D)* and replaces the no-match error on completion. Use first(null, defaultValue) without a predicate. Type-guard and Boolean overloads can narrow the payload; predicates also receive index and source.

operators.name: ignoreElements
operators.behavior: Suppress every next value while preserving the source's completion or error notification.
details: The source is still subscribed and executes normally; ignoring its values does not prevent its side effects.
A source that never terminates leaves the result open. never* describes the absence of next values, not the termination behavior.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(ignoreElements()) // no next values; complete
operators.overloads: The native signature accepts unknown payloads and produces Observable<never>.

operators.name: last
operators.behavior: Remember the latest matching value and emit it when the source completes. Without a predicate, every source value matches.
details: It must wait for normal source completion to know which matching value was last.
If the source completes without a match, the selected form errors with EmptyError.
A source error or downstream unsubscription discards the remembered value.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3, 4).pipe(last(n => n % 2 === 1)) // next: 3 at source completion; complete
operators.overloads: A second argument defaultValue: D changes the output to (A | D)* and replaces the no-match error on completion. Use last(null, defaultValue) without a predicate. Type-guard and Boolean overloads can narrow the payload; predicates also receive index and source.

operators.name: sample
operators.behavior: On each notifier next, emit the latest source value received since the previous sample. If no new source value arrived, emit nothing.
details: Sampling clears the pending-value flag, so repeated notifier values do not replay the same source value.
Notifier completion is ignored. Source completion immediately completes the result without flushing a pending value.
The source is subscribed before the notifier; a synchronous source can finish before the notifier is subscribed.
A notifier error terminates the result, as does a source error.
operators.example: If the source emits 1 then 2 before a notifier next, that next releases 2. A second notifier next with no new source value emits nothing. Source completion then completes the result.
operators.overloads: The notifier also accepts other ObservableInput values. Its emitted payload is ignored.

operators.name: sampleTime
operators.signature: sampleTime(period: number, scheduler?: SchedulerLike): A* => A*
operators.behavior: At regular clock ticks, emit the latest source value received since the previous tick. A tick with no new value produces no output.
details: The sampling clock runs independently of source arrivals; arrivals do not move its next tick.
Source completion immediately completes the result and discards any value waiting for a later tick.
The scheduler defaults to asyncScheduler; period uses its time units, normally milliseconds.
operators.example: With a 10 ms period, values 1 at 2 ms and 2 at 7 ms produce 2 at the 10 ms tick. If the source completes at 15 ms, the result completes then.
operators.overloads: Equivalent to sample(interval(period, scheduler)).

operators.name: single
operators.behavior: Require exactly one matching value across the source. Emit that value only after source completion proves there was no second match.
details: A second match causes an immediate SequenceError, without emitting the first match.
A source that completes without any values causes EmptyError.
A nonempty source that completes with no predicate match causes NotFoundError.
There is no default-value argument. A nonterminating source with only one match still cannot establish uniqueness.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(single(n => n % 2 === 0)) // next: 2 at source completion; complete
operators.overloads: Without a predicate, all source values count as matches. Predicates also receive index and source. A Boolean overload narrows truthy payloads.

operators.name: skip
operators.behavior: Discard the first count source values, then forward later values.
details: Counting is local to each subscription and does not depend on elapsed time.
A source that completes before enough values arrive simply completes without output.
For count zero or below, values pass through.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3, 4).pipe(skip(2)) // next: 3, 4; complete
operators.overloads: The teaching form assumes an integer count.

operators.name: skipLast
operators.behavior: Hold back the latest count values. Each later arrival releases the oldest held value; the final held values are discarded when the source ends.
details: This introduces a lag measured in source values, not a timed delay.
Normal completion does not flush the held values. A source with at most count values completes without emitting.
Positive integer counts retain up to count values; zero or negative counts pass values through.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3, 4).pipe(skipLast(2)) // next: 1 when 3 arrives, 2 when 4 arrives; complete
operators.overloads: The teaching form assumes an integer count.

operators.name: skipUntil
operators.behavior: Discard source values until the notifier sends its first next notification. Forward later source values from then on.
details: The notifier is subscribed before the source, so a synchronous notifier next can open the gate before the first source value.
After opening the gate, the notifier is unsubscribed; it cannot close the gate again.
Notifier completion without next leaves the gate closed. Source completion still completes the result; notifier errors terminate it.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(skipUntil(of('go'))) // next: 1, 2, 3; complete
operators.overloads: The notifier also accepts other ObservableInput values; its payload is ignored.

operators.name: skipWhile
operators.behavior: Discard the initial run of values for which the predicate is true. Emit the first value for which it is false and every later value.
details: The predicate stops being called after its first false result.
Later values pass through even if they would have satisfied the original skipping condition.
If the predicate stays true until source completion, the result completes without values.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3, 1).pipe(skipWhile(n => n < 3)) // next: 3, 1; complete
operators.overloads: The callback also receives a zero-based index. Native overloads include Boolean and an always-true predicate; skipWhile does not generally provide type-guard narrowing for later values.

operators.name: take
operators.behavior: Forward up to count source values, then complete and unsubscribe from the source.
details: A positive count is an upper bound, not a promise that the source will supply that many values.
Early source completion is forwarded without an empty-source error.
For count zero or below, the result completes immediately without subscribing to the source.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(take(2)) // next: 1, 2; complete
operators.overloads: The teaching form assumes an integer count. take(1) permits zero values; first() instead errors if its source completes empty.

operators.name: takeLast
operators.behavior: Remember up to count recent values and emit them in their original order when the source completes.
details: For a positive count, no values are emitted before normal source completion.
If the source supplies fewer than count values and completes, all its values are emitted; an empty source completes without error.
A source error or downstream unsubscription discards the buffered values.
For count zero or below, the result completes immediately without subscribing to the source.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3, 4).pipe(takeLast(2)) // next: 3, 4 at source completion; complete
operators.overloads: The teaching form assumes an integer count. The buffer retains at most count values for a positive integer count.

operators.name: takeUntil
operators.behavior: Forward source values until the notifier sends a next notification. That notification completes the result and tears down both subscriptions.
details: The notifier is subscribed first. A synchronous notifier next prevents the source from being subscribed at all.
Notifier completion without next does not stop the source.
Source completion also completes the result; a source or notifier error terminates it with that error.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(takeUntil(EMPTY)) // next: 1, 2, 3; complete; notifier completion does not stop values
operators.overloads: The notifier also accepts other ObservableInput values; its payload is ignored.

operators.name: takeWhile
operators.signature: takeWhile(predicate: A => boolean, inclusive?: boolean): A* => A*
operators.behavior: Forward the initial run of values that satisfy the predicate. Complete at the first false result, optionally including that boundary value.
details: inclusive defaults to false; true emits the first failing value before completion.
