After the first failure, the source is unsubscribed and no later values are tested.
If the source completes while all tested values pass, completion is forwarded normally.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3, 1).pipe(takeWhile(n => n < 3)) // next: 1, 2; complete when 3 arrives
operators.overloads: The predicate also receives a zero-based index. Type-guard and Boolean overloads can narrow the result when inclusive is false or omitted; including the failing boundary generally preserves A.

operators.name: throttle
operators.signature: throttle(durationSelector: A => unknown*, config?: ThrottleConfig): A* => A*
operators.behavior: Use a duration to limit which values pass during a burst. By default, emit a leading value immediately and suppress further values while its duration is active.
details: Defaults are leading: true and trailing: false. With trailing enabled, remember the latest suppressed value for release on a duration next.
A duration next ends the current gate. A trailing emission starts a new duration while the source is still active.
Duration completion without next ends the gate without a trailing emission.
Source completion waits only if a trailing value is pending behind an active duration; its next releases that value, while completion without next discards it.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(throttle(() => timer(10))) // next: 1; complete
operators.overloads: ThrottleConfig has optional leading and trailing booleans. The duration selector also accepts other ObservableInput values; their payloads are ignored.

operators.name: throttleTime
operators.signature: throttleTime(duration: number, scheduler?: SchedulerLike, config?: ThrottleConfig): A* => A*
operators.behavior: By default, emit a value immediately and suppress new values for a fixed duration. Leading and trailing options choose which ends of each interval may emit.
details: Defaults are leading: true and trailing: false. trailing: true can emit the latest value held during the interval.
Suppressed source values do not restart the running interval. A trailing emission can start the next interval while the source remains active.
If source completion leaves a trailing value pending, the result waits for the timer to release it; the default configuration completes immediately.
The scheduler defaults to asyncScheduler, with time units normally in milliseconds. Errors and downstream unsubscription discard pending values.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(throttleTime(10)) // next: 1; complete
operators.overloads: Equivalent to throttle(() => timer(duration, scheduler), config). ThrottleConfig contains optional leading and trailing booleans.

operators.name: combineLatestAll
operators.behavior: Collect the inner sources until the outer source completes, then combine those sources by their latest values.
details: No inner source is subscribed before outer completion; a never-completing outer prevents all inner subscriptions.
After collection, every inner must provide a first value. Later inner values emit a new array in collected-source order.
A completed inner's latest value remains usable; normal result completion waits for all collected inners to complete.
An empty outer completes without a next value. Hot inner values emitted before the delayed inner subscriptions are not recovered.
operators.example: of(of(1, 2), of(10, 20)).pipe(combineLatestAll()) // next: [2, 10], [2, 20]; complete
operators.overloads: The selected form uses homogeneous Observable<A> inners and produces array values. Native inputs may be other ObservableInput values, and an optional projection can produce B* instead of (A[])*.

operators.name: concatAll
operators.behavior: Subscribe to one inner source at a time. Queue later inner sources and start the next only when the current inner completes.
details: The first inner can start before the outer completes; output follows inner subscription order.
Outer completion waits for the active inner and queued inners to finish. A nonterminating inner blocks the queue.
The queue stores inner sources, not events missed before their subscriptions; hot inner values can be lost while waiting.
A fast outer can grow the queue without bound. Errors terminate the result and discard queued work.
operators.example: of(of(1, 2).pipe(delay(10)), of(3)).pipe(concatAll()) // next: 1, 2, 3; complete
operators.overloads: Equivalent to mergeAll(1). Native inner inputs may also be other ObservableInput values.

operators.name: exhaustAll
operators.behavior: Subscribe to an inner source only when no inner is active. Ignore new inner sources while the current one is running.
details: Ignored inner sources are neither subscribed nor queued for later.
When the active inner completes, the next outer value can supply a new inner.
Outer completion waits for the active inner. A nonterminating active inner keeps the result open.
operators.example: of(of(1, 2).pipe(delay(10)), of(3)).pipe(exhaustAll()) // next: 1, 2; complete; of(3) is ignored
operators.overloads: Native inner inputs may also be other ObservableInput values. exhaust is the deprecated earlier name.

operators.name: mergeAll
operators.behavior: Subscribe to inner sources as they arrive, up to the concurrency limit, and forward values from all active inners.
details: concurrent defaults to Infinity. A positive limit queues additional inner sources until an active inner completes.
Values follow actual arrival order across active inners; earlier outer positions do not reserve earlier output positions.
Outer completion waits for all active and queued inners to finish.
The limit bounds active subscriptions, not queue length. Errors cancel active inners and discard queued work.
operators.example: of(of(1, 2).pipe(delay(10)), of(3)).pipe(mergeAll()) // next: 3, 1, 2; complete
operators.overloads: Use a positive integer limit or Infinity. Native inner inputs may also be other ObservableInput values; mergeAll(1) has concatAll's policy.

operators.name: switchAll
operators.behavior: Follow only the latest inner source. Each new inner replaces the previous inner subscription immediately.
details: The previous inner is unsubscribed before its replacement is subscribed; already emitted values remain part of the output history.
Outer completion waits for the current inner to complete; it does not cancel that final inner.
Stopping underlying external work depends on the inner source's teardown implementation.
operators.example: of(of(1, 2).pipe(delay(10)), of(3)).pipe(switchAll()) // next: 3; complete; the delayed inner is unsubscribed
operators.overloads: Equivalent to switchMap(inner => inner). Native inner inputs may also be other ObservableInput values.

operators.name: startWith
operators.behavior: On subscription, emit the supplied values in order, then subscribe to the source and forward its values.
details: In the selected form, the supplied values are emitted synchronously before the source subscription starts.
If downstream closes while receiving those initial values, the source need not be subscribed.
Argument expressions are evaluated when constructing the operator. Use defer when a starting value must be computed anew per subscription.
operators.example: of(2, 3).pipe(startWith(0, 1)) // next: 0, 1, 2, 3; complete
operators.overloads: The variadic native form preserves unions of heterogeneous initial values, including null and undefined. Only the scheduler-argument overload is deprecated; startWith itself is current.

operators.name: withLatestFrom
operators.behavior: When the primary source emits A, pair it with the latest B from the companion. Companion values update the remembered B without triggering output.
details: Every companion must have emitted once before a primary value can produce a tuple; early primary values are discarded.
Companions are subscribed before the primary source. A synchronous companion can establish its latest value during setup.
Companion completion does not complete the result. A completed companion's last value remains available; a companion that completes empty never establishes readiness.
Primary completion completes the result and unsubscribes companions; an error from any subscribed input terminates it.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(withLatestFrom(of('a', 'b'))) // next: [1, 'b'], [2, 'b']; complete
operators.overloads: The selected form has one Observable companion. Native forms accept multiple ObservableInput companions and an optional projection; output tuples keep the primary value first.

operators.name: combineAll
operators.behavior: Collect inner sources until outer completion, then emit arrays of their latest values. This is the older name for combineLatestAll.
details: Inner subscriptions begin only after the outer completes.
Each collected inner must emit before any combined array can be emitted; later arrays retain collected-source order.
Normal completion waits for all collected inner sources; an empty outer completes without emitting.
operators.example: of(of(1, 2), of(10, 20)).pipe(combineAll()) // next: [2, 10], [2, 20]; complete
operators.overloads: The function is a direct alias of combineLatestAll, including its ObservableInput and projection overloads.

operators.name: combineLatest
operators.behavior: Combine the primary source with companions so every input update emits their latest-value tuple once all inputs have emitted.
details: This is the legacy pipeable import from rxjs/operators; the creation function exported by rxjs is a separate API.
Completed inputs retain their latest values; normal completion waits for all inputs. An empty-completing input prevents readiness without forcing immediate completion in RxJS 7.8.2.
The primary source is subscribed before its companions, which affects synchronous examples.
operators.example:
import { combineLatest as combineLatestOperator } from 'rxjs/operators';
of(1, 2).pipe(combineLatestOperator(of('a', 'b'))) // next: [2, 'a'], [2, 'b']; complete
operators.overloads: Legacy forms accept an array or separate ObservableInput companions and an optional projection. Prefer combineLatestWith followed by map for a projected result.

operators.name: combineLatestWith
operators.behavior: After both inputs have supplied a value, any new value from either input emits a tuple containing their latest values.
details: The primary source is subscribed first, followed by companions in argument order; synchronous inputs can finish during setup.
A completed input's last value remains usable. Normal result completion waits for all inputs to complete.
In RxJS 7.8.2, an input that completes empty prevents tuples but does not itself force immediate result completion; another input can keep the result open.
A source error terminates the result and unsubscribes the other inputs.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(combineLatestWith(of('a', 'b'))) // next: [2, 'a'], [2, 'b']; complete
operators.overloads: The native variadic form accepts several ObservableInput companions and produces [A, B, C, ...]* in source order.

operators.name: concat
operators.behavior: Forward the primary source, then subscribe to each supplied companion in order after the previous source completes.
details: This is the legacy pipeable import from rxjs/operators, distinct from the concat creation function.
A nonterminating input blocks later subscriptions; an error ends the sequence.
Hot companion values sent before the companion's turn are not retained.
operators.example:
import { concat as concatOperator } from 'rxjs/operators';
of(1, 2).pipe(concatOperator(of('a'))) // next: 1, 2, 'a'; complete
operators.overloads: Legacy forms accept multiple ObservableInput companions and an optional final scheduler. Use concatWith for the selected unscheduled form.

operators.name: concatWith
operators.behavior: Forward the primary source, then subscribe to the companion after the primary completes and forward the companion.
details: With multiple companions, subscriptions proceed in argument order, one at a time.
A source that never completes blocks later subscriptions; an error ends the sequence without moving on.
Values from a hot companion before its turn are not buffered by concatWith.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(concatWith(of('a', 'b'))) // next: 1, 2, 'a', 'b'; complete
operators.overloads: The native form accepts multiple ObservableInput companions. The output payload is the union of their value types and the primary source's value type.

operators.name: endWith
operators.behavior: Forward the source, then emit the supplied values in order after normal source completion and complete the result.
details: In the selected form, the appended values are emitted synchronously when source completion is received.
A source error or downstream unsubscription does not emit the appended values.
A source that never completes never reaches the appended values.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(endWith('done')) // next: 1, 2, 'done'; complete
operators.overloads: The native variadic form preserves unions of heterogeneous appended values. The scheduler-argument behavior is deprecated; endWith itself is current.

operators.name: merge
operators.replacement: mergeWith for the common unlimited-concurrency form; use merge or mergeAll for an explicit concurrency limit
operators.behavior: Subscribe to the primary and companion sources and interleave their arriving values into one result.
details: This is the legacy pipeable import from rxjs/operators, distinct from the merge creation function.
The selected form starts inputs in source order and permits overlapping subscriptions without a concurrency limit.
Normal completion waits for all inputs; an input error terminates the result and cancels the others.
operators.example:
import { merge as mergeOperator } from 'rxjs/operators';
of(1, 2).pipe(delay(10), mergeOperator(of('a'))) // next: 'a', 1, 2; complete
operators.overloads: Legacy forms accept multiple ObservableInput companions, an optional concurrency number, and an optional scheduler. Those extra options are not parameters of mergeWith.

operators.name: mergeWith
operators.behavior: Subscribe to the primary and companion sources and forward each input's values as they arrive.
details: Subscriptions start in primary-then-companion order, so a synchronous input can emit during setup before later inputs are subscribed.
Normal completion waits for every input to complete.
An error from any input terminates the result and unsubscribes the others.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(delay(10), mergeWith(of('a'))) // next: 'a', 1, 2; complete
operators.overloads: The native form accepts multiple ObservableInput companions. For an explicit concurrency limit, use an appropriate merge creation form or a higher-order source with mergeAll(limit).

operators.name: race
operators.behavior: Race the primary and companion sources: the first next chooses a source to follow, while a first complete or error ends the result immediately.
details: This is the legacy pipeable import from rxjs/operators, distinct from the race creation function.
Losing subscriptions are closed; a synchronous winner can prevent later inputs from being subscribed.
An empty input can end the race before any value is emitted.
operators.example:
import { race as raceOperator } from 'rxjs/operators';
of(1, 2).pipe(raceOperator(of('later'))) // next: 1, 2; complete
operators.overloads: Legacy forms accept an array or separate ObservableInput companions. The implementation delegates to raceWith.

operators.name: raceWith
operators.behavior: Let the first input notification decide the result. A first next selects that source for the remaining output; a first complete or error ends the result immediately.
details: Once a source wins with a next value, other subscribed inputs are unsubscribed.
Inputs are subscribed in primary-then-companion order. A synchronous winner can prevent later inputs from being subscribed at all.
An empty source can win by completing before any competing value arrives.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(raceWith(of('later'))) // next: 1, 2; complete; the companion is never subscribed
operators.overloads: The native form accepts multiple ObservableInput companions. With no companions, raceWith() returns the primary source unchanged.

operators.name: zip
operators.behavior: Combine equally numbered values from the primary and companion sources into tuples, waiting until every input has its next unpaired value.
details: This is the legacy pipeable import from rxjs/operators, distinct from the zip creation function.
Faster inputs are queued; completion occurs when a completed input has no queued values left.
Queue growth depends on differences in input rates, so a slow companion can retain many primary values.
operators.example:
import { zip as zipOperator } from 'rxjs/operators';
of(1, 2, 3).pipe(zipOperator(of('a', 'b'))) // next: [1, 'a'], [2, 'b']; complete
operators.overloads: Legacy forms accept multiple ObservableInput companions and optional projection overloads. Prefer zipWith followed by map for a projected result.

operators.name: zipAll
operators.behavior: Collect inner sources until the outer completes, then combine their first values, second values, and later matching positions into arrays.
details: No inner is subscribed before outer completion; a nonterminating outer prevents the join from starting.
Array positions follow the order in which inner sources were collected, while each inner's unpaired values wait in a queue.
The result completes when any completed inner has no queued value left. An empty outer completes without a next value.
Hot inner values sent before the eventual subscriptions are missed, and faster subscribed inners can grow their queues.
operators.example: of(of(1, 2), of(10, 20, 30)).pipe(zipAll()) // next: [1, 10], [2, 20]; complete
operators.overloads: The selected form uses homogeneous Observable<A> inners. Native inputs may be other ObservableInput values; an optional projection changes the output from (A[])* to B*.

operators.name: zipWith
operators.behavior: Pair the first value from each input, then the second from each, and so on. Emit a tuple whenever every input has its next unpaired value available.
details: Values from faster inputs wait in queues; these queues can grow when arrival rates differ.
A completed input can still contribute values already queued.
The result completes as soon as a completed input has no queued value left, because another full tuple is impossible. An input that completes empty can therefore end the result immediately.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(zipWith(of('a', 'b'))) // next: [1, 'a'], [2, 'b']; complete
operators.overloads: The native variadic form accepts multiple ObservableInput companions and emits tuples in primary-then-companion order.

operators.name: multicast
operators.behavior: Routes one connected source execution through a Subject chosen by the caller. The returned legacy connectable exposes explicit connection control.
details: Subscribing to the result attaches a listener; connect() starts the source connection. Unsubscribing the connection tears that connection down.
A Subject instance reuses that instance; a factory can supply a new one when the legacy connectable recreates its subject. The Subject type controls replay and terminal behavior.
operators.overloads: The selector overload, multicast(connector, shared => result), returns B* and shares within that selector instead of exposing connect().
operators.replacement: connectable(source, { connector }) for explicit connections; connect(selector, { connector }) for selector-local sharing.

operators.name: publish
operators.behavior: Creates a legacy connectable backed by one plain Subject, sharing live values without replay.
details: Listeners can attach before connect() starts the source. The plain Subject has no cached next value for a late listener.
The no-selector form reuses its Subject. Its completed or errored Subject is retained for later listeners.
operators.overloads: publish(selector: A* => B*) returns A* => B*; use connect(selector) for that form.
operators.replacement: connectable(source, { connector: () => new Subject(), resetOnDisconnect: false }) for the legacy connection policy; share() for default automatic sharing.

operators.name: publishBehavior
operators.behavior: Creates a legacy connectable backed by a BehaviorSubject. While the subject is active, a listener immediately receives its current value, initially the seed.
details: The seed can be observed before connect() starts the source; source values subsequently replace the current value.
A late listener after completion receives only complete, not the cached value. After error it receives that error.
operators.replacement: connectable(source, { connector: () => new BehaviorSubject(seed), resetOnDisconnect: false }); choose share configuration explicitly for automatic connections.

operators.name: publishLast
operators.behavior: Creates a legacy connectable backed by an AsyncSubject. It remembers the latest source value and publishes that value only when the source completes normally.
details: An empty source completes without a next value; a source error is forwarded without publishing the remembered value.
After successful completion, late listeners receive the final value and complete. Before completion, source values are withheld.
operators.replacement: connectable(source, { connector: () => new AsyncSubject(), resetOnDisconnect: false }).

operators.name: publishReplay
operators.signature: publishReplay(bufferSize?: number, windowTime?: number): A* => ConnectableObservable<A>
operators.behavior: Creates a legacy connectable backed by one ReplaySubject. New listeners first receive eligible cached values, then live values.
details: The buffer is limited by count and age; both defaults are unbounded. connect() starts the source; replay itself does not start it.
The same ReplaySubject is retained, including its completion or error. Cached values within the retention limits can be replayed before that terminal notification.
operators.overloads: This card shows runtime connectability. The no-selector public overload is typed only as MonoTypeOperatorFunction<A>, so TypeScript can require the cast shown. Selector and timestamp-provider overloads also exist.
operators.replacement: connectable(source, { connector: () => new ReplaySubject(bufferSize, windowTime), resetOnDisconnect: false }); shareReplay has different reset defaults.

operators.name: share
operators.behavior: Shares a source connection among listeners attached to the same shared Observable instance. The default connector is a plain Subject, so it forwards live values without replay.
details: By default the first listener connects, and losing the last listener disconnects an active source. Error, completion, and a zero listener count each reset the sharing state.
Separate subscriptions to a synchronously completing shared source can each start a new execution because the first execution has already completed and reset.
The configuration changes the connector and reset policies; it can retain a terminal state or delay a reset.
operators.example:
const shared$ = interval(1000).pipe(share());
// Overlapping subscriptions to shared$ use one interval connection.
operators.overloads: The signature preserves payload type; sharing is a connection policy, not a property of A* itself.

operators.name: connect
operators.signature: connect(selector: A* => B*, config?: ConnectConfig<A>): A* => B*
operators.behavior: Gives a selector a shared view of the source, then connects the source after the selected result has been subscribed. This lets several branches observe one source execution within that result subscription.
details: A new connector is made for each subscription to the resulting Observable. This does not automatically share across separate result subscriptions.
The default connector is a plain Subject. The selected result supplies the output type and termination policy; tearing down the result also tears down its source connection.
operators.overloads: The actual selector may return any ObservableInput<B>. ConnectConfig<A> requires a connector when a config object is supplied.

operators.name: connectable
operators.behavior: Create a shared stream with an explicit connection switch. Subscribers attach to the shared subject; connect() starts the source subscription.
details: The default connector creates a plain Subject, so it does not replay earlier values to later subscribers.
connect() returns the shared connection Subscription. Unsubscribing that connection disconnects the source; merely having no observers does not automatically disconnect it.
By default, resetOnDisconnect is true: ending a connection replaces the subject for future subscriptions and connections. Existing observers are not moved to the replacement subject.
Attach observers before connecting when synchronous source values must reach them.
operators.overloads: The actual source may be ObservableInput. Connectable<A> is an A* with connect(): Subscription. A supplied config provides a connector factory and may select resetOnDisconnect; replay requires an appropriate connector.

operators.name: refCount
operators.behavior: Adds listener-count control to a legacy ConnectableObservable: connect for the first listener and disconnect an active shared connection after the last listener leaves.
details: The connector and its retained terminal state come from the preceding legacy multicasting operation; refCount does not add replay or choose reset behavior.

This teaching input names the legacy connectable requirement even though the public TypeScript return type is MonoTypeOperatorFunction<A>. Do not treat it as a generic adapter for the newer connectable() result.
operators.example:
const shared$ = interval(1000).pipe(publish(), refCount());
// Legacy automatic connection pattern; prefer share().
operators.replacement: share(), with an explicit connector/reset configuration when preserving legacy behavior.

operators.name: shareReplay
operators.behavior: Shares through a ReplaySubject so late listeners receive eligible cached values before live values.
details: Prefer an explicit bufferSize and refCount. With refCount: true, losing the last listener resets and disconnects an active source; refCount: false keeps that active connection.
In RxJS 7.8.2, an error resets the shared state, but successful completion retains the replay cache. refCount: true does not clear a successfully completed cache.
windowTime limits the age of replayed values; expiration is checked by the ReplaySubject and does not by itself trigger a new source execution.
operators.overloads: The positional overload shareReplay(bufferSize?, windowTime?, scheduler?) defaults refCount to false. The scheduler supplies the replay timestamp clock; it does not schedule delivery of cached values.

operators.name: catchError
operators.behavior: Forwards source values until an error, then replaces the failed subscription with the Observable returned by recover.
details: Values emitted before the error remain in the output. Returning a fallback does not undo those values or resume the failed source.
A thrown recovery error, or an error from the replacement, propagates downstream. Unsubscription tears down whichever subscription is active.
operators.overloads: The actual callback receives (error, caught) and returns ObservableInput<B>. Returning caught requests resubscription through the same catchError logic.

operators.name: retry
operators.behavior: On source error, subscribes to the source again, up to the retry policy. Every attempt can contribute values to the same output.
details: retry(2) allows the original subscription plus two retries. The default count is unbounded; count <= 0 does not retry. Completion is forwarded normally.
A delay may be a duration or an error/count callback. The first delay-notifier next retries; completion without a next completes the result, and a notifier error errors it.
resetOnSuccess resets the retry counter on a next value, not on completion; it defaults to false. Resubscription repeats source side effects.
operators.example: defer(() => of(1)).pipe(retry(2)) // next: 1; complete; no retry needed
operators.overloads: RetryConfig contains count?, delay?, and resetOnSuccess?. The callback retry count starts at 1.

operators.name: retryWhen
operators.behavior: Feeds source errors into a notifier factory. Notifier next values request new subscriptions to the source.
details: The notifier is created after the first source error. Its output controls retries; its own next payload is ignored.
Notifier completion completes the result and notifier error errors it. Ordinary source completion completes the result without requiring notifier completion.
operators.example:
request$.pipe(retryWhen(errors$ => errors$.pipe(delay(1000))))
// After each source error, the notifier requests a retry after 1 second.
operators.overloads: The notifier may return any ObservableInput. Errors are typed unknown in this teaching view instead of the public any.
operators.replacement: retry({ delay: (error, retryCount) => retrySignal$ }) for the usual retry policy; translate custom notifier state deliberately.

operators.name: onErrorResumeNext
operators.behavior: The legacy pipeable name for onErrorResumeNextWith. It advances to the next input when the current input completes or errors.
details: This entry is the rxjs/operators export. The same name imported from rxjs is a creation function that takes all sources directly.
Errors from constituent inputs are swallowed; a nonterminating input prevents progression.
operators.example:
// import { onErrorResumeNext } from 'rxjs/operators';
throwError(() => new Error('failed')).pipe(onErrorResumeNext(of(2))) // next: 2; complete

operators.name: onErrorResumeNextWith
operators.behavior: Concatenates subscriptions, advancing to the next input after either normal completion or error. Errors from the constituent inputs are swallowed.
details: Inputs are subscribed sequentially. An input that never terminates prevents reaching later inputs.
There is no recovery callback and no error value to inspect here; use catchError when the error should determine the fallback.
operators.example:
throwError(() => new Error('failed')).pipe(onErrorResumeNextWith(of('next')))
// next: 'next'; complete
operators.overloads: Variadic and array input forms accept ObservableInput values and produce the union of input payloads.

operators.name: tap
operators.behavior: Runs an effect for each source value and forwards that same value. The callback return value is ignored.
details: A synchronous exception in the next-value callback becomes an error downstream. Teardown hooks have teardown-error behavior instead. Callbacks can still mutate referenced objects.
tap does not start a subscription by itself. Its observer-object form also provides error, complete, subscribe, unsubscribe, and finalize hooks.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(tap(n => console.log(n))) // next: 1, 2; complete; also logs each value
operators.overloads: Use an observer object for multiple hooks. The older separate next/error/complete-argument overload is deprecated; tap itself is current.

operators.name: delay
operators.signature: delay(due: number | Date, scheduler?: SchedulerLike): A* => A*
operators.behavior: Holds source values until their scheduled release time. A numeric due delays each value by that duration; a Date is an absolute release time.
details: The default scheduler is asyncScheduler. The source is subscribed immediately; this delays delivery, not the start of source work.
Completion waits for held values. A source error is forwarded immediately and discards held values; unsubscription also discards them.
An empty source can complete immediately: delay does not simply shift every terminal notification by the due time.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(delay(100)) // after about 100 ms: next 1, 2; complete

operators.name: delayWhen
operators.behavior: Creates a release Observable for each source value. The first next from that Observable releases that value.
details: Each value has its own subscription, so later source values can be released first. Output order need not match source order.
A release Observable that completes without a next drops its value in RxJS 7.8.2. Source completion waits for outstanding releases; errors terminate and discard pending values.
operators.example:
of(1, 2).pipe(delayWhen(n => timer(n === 1 ? 20 : 10)))
// next: 2 at about 10 ms, 1 at about 20 ms; complete
operators.overloads: The actual callback also receives an index and may return ObservableInput. The deprecated subscriptionDelay overload gates the initial source subscription on notifier next or completion.

operators.name: dematerialize
operators.behavior: Interprets notification objects as real next, error, and complete notifications.
details: An N notice emits its value. An E notice errors the result; a C notice completes it. Either terminal notice ends the subscription and prevents later notices from being delivered.
The input stream can also terminate through its own error or completion channel; a terminal notice is not required.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(materialize(), dematerialize()) // next: 1, 2; complete
operators.overloads: The actual input is ObservableNotification<A>, including structurally compatible objects. The output type extracts the value of N notices.

operators.name: materialize
operators.behavior: Turns next, error, and complete notifications into ordinary next values describing those notifications.
details: A source error becomes one E notice followed by normal completion of the materialized result. Normal source completion becomes one C notice followed by completion.
Unsubscription creates no notice. Materializing an outer stream does not materialize notifications inside its inner streams.
operators.example:
of(1).pipe(materialize()) // next: N(1), C; complete
// N(1) and C describe notification objects here, not function calls.
operators.overloads: Notice<A> denotes the observable-notification union. Runtime results are Notification<A> instances that also satisfy ObservableNotification<A>.

operators.name: observeOn
operators.signature: observeOn(scheduler: SchedulerLike, delay?: number): A* => A*
operators.behavior: Schedules delivery of next, error, and complete notifications to the downstream listener.
details: It does not schedule when source subscription begins or move source work to another thread. The chosen scheduler determines execution timing.
Delay defaults to 0. Unsubscription cancels pending scheduled deliveries. Unlike delay, an error is scheduled too.
operators.example:
of(1, 2).pipe(observeOn(asyncScheduler))
// Schedules next 1, next 2, and complete after the current synchronous work.

operators.name: subscribeOn
operators.signature: subscribeOn(scheduler: SchedulerLike, delay?: number): A* => A*
operators.behavior: Schedules the act of subscribing to the source, including the work performed as that subscription starts.
details: Once the source starts, its own behavior determines how values are delivered. This is not a per-notification scheduling policy.
Delay defaults to 0. Unsubscribing before the scheduled subscription runs cancels it, so source work does not start.
operators.example:
defer(() => of(1, 2)).pipe(subscribeOn(asyncScheduler))
// The factory is called when the scheduled source subscription runs.

operators.name: timeInterval
operators.signature: timeInterval(scheduler?: SchedulerLike): A* => { value: A; interval: number }*
operators.behavior: Pairs each source value with the elapsed clock time since the preceding source value, or since subscription for the first value.
details: The default clock is asyncScheduler.now(). interval is a duration, not an absolute timestamp.
The operator measures time without delaying values or scheduling source work. Clock units follow the supplied scheduler.
operators.example:
interval(100).pipe(take(2), timeInterval())
// Values 0 and 1 are wrapped with intervals of about 100 ms each.
operators.overloads: The actual result is a TimeInterval<A> object with these public fields.

operators.name: timestamp
operators.signature: timestamp(clock?: TimestampProvider): A* => { value: A; timestamp: number }*
operators.behavior: Pairs each source value with the current clock reading at the point this operator receives it.
details: By default the clock uses Date.now(). timestamp is an absolute clock reading, unlike the elapsed duration from timeInterval.
A custom TimestampProvider only needs now(). Reading a clock neither delays delivery nor changes source scheduling.
operators.example:
of("ready").pipe(timestamp())
// next: { value: "ready", timestamp: currentClockReading }; complete
operators.overloads: The actual result type is Timestamp<A>. A SchedulerLike can serve as a TimestampProvider.

operators.name: timeout
operators.signature:
timeout(due: number | Date, scheduler?: SchedulerLike): A* => A*
timeout(config: TimeoutConfig<A, B*> & { with: TimeoutInfo<A> => B* }): A* => (A | B)*
operators.behavior: Enforces a deadline for receiving a source value. On expiry it unsubscribes the source and either errors or switches to a configured fallback.
details: For a positive numeric due, the deadline covers the first value and every following gap. A Date overload sets only the first-value deadline. asyncScheduler is the default scheduler.
The config separates first and each. Without with, expiry raises TimeoutError; with supplies the replacement subscription. Values already forwarded remain in the result.
The fallback is not recursively checked by the same timeout. Completion or error before a deadline ends the source normally for that channel.
operators.example:
NEVER.pipe(timeout({ first: 100, with: () => of("fallback") }))
// next: "fallback" at about 100 ms; complete
operators.overloads: At least first or each is required at runtime. The full API accepts ObservableInput fallbacks and metadata. The zero/negative each edge is not represented by the positive-duration teaching rule.

operators.name: timeoutWith
operators.signature: timeoutWith(due: number | Date, fallback: B*, scheduler?: SchedulerLike): A* => (A | B)*
operators.behavior: The older timeout form that switches to a supplied fallback when a source-value deadline expires.
details: A positive number guards the first value and subsequent gaps; a Date guards the first value only.
On expiry the source is unsubscribed and fallback is subscribed. Previously delivered values remain in the output.
operators.example:
NEVER.pipe(timeoutWith(100, of("fallback")))
// next: "fallback" at about 100 ms; complete
operators.overloads: The actual fallback may be any ObservableInput<B>.
operators.replacement: timeout({ each: duration, with: () => fallback }) or timeout({ first: date, with: () => fallback }).

operators.name: toArray
operators.behavior: Collects source values into one array and emits that array when the source completes normally.
details: An empty completed source emits [] once. Source errors and unsubscription discard the accumulated array.
A source that never completes never emits its array. Memory use grows with the number of collected values.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(toArray()) // next: [1, 2, 3]; complete
operators.overloads: The result is a stream carrying an array value; it is not an array of Observables.

operators.name: finalize
operators.behavior: Registers cleanup for the subscription. It runs when that subscription ends through completion, error, or unsubscription.
details: The callback receives no reason or last value. It is not a complete callback: cancellation also runs it.
Placement around sharing matters: upstream cleanup follows the shared source connection; downstream cleanup follows each listener subscription.
operators.example:
NEVER.pipe(finalize(() => console.log("released"))).subscribe().unsubscribe();
// No next or complete; logs "released" during teardown.

operators.name: repeat
operators.behavior: On normal source completion, subscribes again according to the repeat policy. Source errors still terminate the result.
details: repeat(3) means three total source subscriptions, including the first. The default is unbounded; count <= 0 completes without subscribing to the source.
A delay may be a duration or a completed-run-count callback. Its first next starts the next run; completion without a next ends repetition.
Resubscription repeats source side effects. Unbounded repetition of a synchronous source needs particular care; it need not yield execution.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(repeat(2)) // next: 1, 2, 1, 2; complete
operators.overloads: RepeatConfig contains count? and delay?. The delay callback first receives 1 after the first run completes.

operators.name: repeatWhen
operators.behavior: Feeds source completion signals into a notifier factory. Each notifier next requests another source subscription.
details: Source errors are forwarded. Notifier errors also error the result.
Notifier completion stops requesting new runs; the result completes once the active source run has also completed. This differs from retryWhen notifier completion.
With synchronous sources and synchronous notifier completion, notification order can prevent a requested repeat from starting. Test that boundary when translating legacy notifier logic.
operators.example:
timer(10).pipe(repeatWhen(completions$ => completions$.pipe(take(1))))
// next: 0, then 0 from the repeated run; complete
operators.overloads: The void values are next notifications signalling completed runs, not the completion channel itself. The actual notifier return type is ObservableInput.
operators.replacement: repeat({ delay: completedRunCount => repeatSignal$ }) for the usual repetition policy.

operators.name: defaultIfEmpty
operators.behavior: Forwards source values. If the source completes normally without any value, it emits the fallback before completing.
details: null and undefined are ordinary values and therefore prevent the fallback from being emitted.
It does not recover errors and does not impose a timeout on a silent, open source.
operators.example: EMPTY.pipe(defaultIfEmpty("none")) // next: "none"; complete

operators.name: every
operators.behavior: Emits false and completes at the first value that fails the predicate. If all received values pass and the source completes, it emits true.
details: An empty completed source emits true. An open source whose values all pass has not yet established true.
The first failing value ends the subscription early. Predicate exceptions error the result.
operators.example: of(2, 4, 5, 6).pipe(every(n => n % 2 === 0)) // next: false; complete at 5
operators.overloads: The actual predicate also receives index and source. Boolean-constructor overloads are omitted.

operators.name: find
operators.behavior: Emits the first matching value and completes. If the source completes without a match, it emits undefined and completes.
details: A successful match unsubscribes early. A nonterminating source with no match can remain open indefinitely.
undefined is a delivered payload here, not an empty stream. It is indistinguishable by value from a matched undefined unless the domain supplies a tag.
operators.example: of(1, 3).pipe(find(n => n % 2 === 0)) // next: undefined; complete
operators.overloads: Type-guard predicates narrow the successful payload to B; the result still includes undefined. Index and source callback parameters are omitted.

operators.name: findIndex
operators.behavior: Emits the zero-based index of the first matching source value and completes. If the source completes with no match, it emits -1.
details: The index counts all received source values, including those that do not match.
A match ends the source subscription early; without a match, normal completion is needed to conclude -1.
operators.example: of("a", "b", "c").pipe(findIndex(x => x === "b")) // next: 1; complete
operators.overloads: The actual predicate also receives index and source.

operators.name: isEmpty
operators.behavior: Emits false and completes as soon as a source value arrives. Emits true only when the source completes without a value.
details: A source error before a value is an error, not true. A silent source that never completes leaves the result open.
The false outcome needs only the first value and cancels further source delivery.
operators.example: of(undefined).pipe(isEmpty()) // next: false; complete

operators.name: sequenceEqual
operators.signature: sequenceEqual(other: A*, equal?: (A, A) => boolean): A* => boolean*
operators.behavior: Compares the two sequences by value position, ignoring differences in their emission times. It emits one boolean once equality or inequality can be decided.
details: Both streams must complete with matching lengths and values to establish true. A mismatching pair or an extra value after the other completes can establish false early.
The default equality is ===. Faster input values are buffered while awaiting partners, so a large rate imbalance can grow memory.
operators.example: of(1, 2).pipe(sequenceEqual(of(1, 2))) // next: true; complete
operators.overloads: The actual comparison input may be ObservableInput<A>.

operators.name: throwIfEmpty
operators.behavior: Passes source values through, but replaces an empty normal completion with an error.
details: The default factory creates EmptyError. It runs only if completion arrives before any next value.
This does not impose a deadline: a source that stays open without values keeps the result open.
operators.example: EMPTY.pipe(throwIfEmpty()) // no next; error: EmptyError

operators.name: count
operators.behavior: Counts received source values, or only the values satisfying a predicate, and emits the total on normal completion.
details: An empty completed source emits 0. No running counts are emitted.
A source error prevents a final count. Use scan when the lesson requires a running count.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3, 4).pipe(count(n => n % 2 === 0)) // next: 2; complete
operators.overloads: The optional predicate also receives the zero-based source index.

operators.name: max
operators.behavior: Remembers the greatest source value and emits it on normal completion.
details: An empty completed source emits no value. No running maximum is emitted before completion.
Without a comparer it uses JavaScript >. A comparer returns a positive number when its first argument should rank higher; ties select the later value in RxJS 7.8.2.
operators.example: of(3, 1, 5, 2).pipe(max()) // next: 5; complete

operators.name: min
operators.behavior: Remembers the least source value and emits it on normal completion.
details: An empty completed source emits no value. No running minimum is emitted before completion.
Without a comparer it uses JavaScript <. A comparer returns a negative number when its first argument should rank lower; ties select the later value in RxJS 7.8.2.
operators.example: of(3, 1, 5, 2).pipe(min()) // next: 1; complete

operators.name: reduce
operators.signature: reduce(reducer: (S, A) => S, seed: S): A* => S*
operators.behavior: Updates accumulated state for each source value, then emits only the final state on normal completion.
details: With the seed shown here, an empty completed source emits the seed once. scan with the same seed emits nothing for that empty source.
The seed is an initial value, not a deep clone; use an immutable reducer. Error or unsubscription prevents the final state from being emitted.
operators.example: of(1, 2, 3).pipe(reduce((sum, n) => sum + n, 0)) // next: 6; complete
operators.overloads: Without a seed, the first input initializes state without calling the reducer. In RxJS 7.8.2 an empty source with that overload completes without a value. The reducer also receives an index.
